mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS increase is < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) by at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting optimism about labor market strength.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the job gain threshold being met (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,000 in monthly units for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating robust consumer demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the double-month high in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2.0 points is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days, reflecting weak manufacturing momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not negative or the INDPRO decline is < 2.0 points.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment) by 0.1% or more predict a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, as dual softening reduces rate-sensitive discounting.
regime_hint: Dual softening in monetary policy and labor markets
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the dual decline, or proxies do not meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS (retail sales in millions) by 10% or more for three months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting robust retail activity.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the 3-month acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to inflation risk premia.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the CPI spike, or CPI increase is < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a 'late-cycle expansion' as signaled by a 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP) above 105 (2017 chain dollars) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return due to optimism about economic momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the late-cycle signal, or MA3(GDPC1) never exceeds 105 in the observation window.
